Bureau of Economic Analysis

November 25, 2026

Split GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026 and Personal Income and Outlays, October 2026

GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026

Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 4.3 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the second estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased.

 Current Release

 Personal Income and Outlays, October 2026

Personal income increased $201.8 billion (0.7 percent at a monthly rate) in October, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Disposable personal income (DPI)—personal income less personal current taxes—increased $200.5 billion (0.8 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $63.8 billion (0.3 percent). Personal outlays—the sum of PCE, personal interest payments, and personal current transfer payments—increased $69.3 billion in October. Personal saving was $1.00 trillion, and the personal saving rate—personal saving as a percentage of DPI—was 4.1 percent.

 Current Release

Activities of U.S. Multinational Enterprises, 2024

November 20, 2026 | News Release

Worldwide employment by U.S. multinational enterprises increased 0.9 percent to 44.2 million workers in 2024 (preliminary) from 43.8 million workers in 2023 (revised), according to statistics released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis on the operations and finances of U.S. parent companies and their majority-owned foreign affiliates.

Read More 

Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S. and States, 2025

November 18, 2026 | News Release

The value added of the outdoor recreation economy accounted for 2.3 percent ($704.2 billion) of current-dollar gross domestic product (GDP) for the nation in 2025. Across states and the District of Columbia, value added for outdoor recreation as a share of state GDP ranged from 6.1 percent in Hawaii to 1.0 percent in the District of Columbia.

Read More 

U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, September 2026

November 4, 2026 | News Release

The U.S. goods and services trade deficit decreased in September 2026 according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and the U.S. Census Bureau. The deficit decreased from $105.7 billion in August (revised) to $105.0 billion in September, as exports increased more than imports. The goods deficit decreased $0.7 billion in September to $135.9 billion. The services surplus decreased less than $0.1 billion in September to $30.9 billion.

Read More 

We Want Your Feedback on BEA Data Tools

November 2, 2026 | The BEA Wire

The Bureau of Economic Analysis is planning to modernize our data dissemination tools, particularly our Application Programming Interface (API) and interactive data tables.

Read More

Real gross domestic product (GDP) increased at an annual rate of 3.4 percent in the third quarter of 2026 (July, August, and September), according to the advance estimate released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). In the second quarter, real GDP increased 2.2 percent. Personal income increased $54.5 billion (0.2 percent at a monthly rate) in September, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). Disposable personal income (DPI)—personal income less personal current taxes—increased $52.7 billion (0.2 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $113.1 billion (0.5 percent). Personal outlays—the sum of PCE, personal interest payments, and personal…

Read More 

State Spotlight: Consumer Spending Increased in All States in 2025

October 7, 2026 | The BEA Wire

BEA’s latest look at state consumer spending shows increases in all 50 states and the District of Columbia in 2025. Spending increased the most in Florida, at 7.0 percent, and the least in California, at 4.2 percent. 

In comparison, consumer spending—also called personal consumption expenditures, or PCE—increased 5.3 percent nationwide in 2025. These numbers are based on current dollars (not adjusted for inflation). 

Read More 

U.S. International Trade in Goods and Services, August 2026

October 6, 2026 | News Release

The U.S. goods and services trade deficit increased in August 2026 according to the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and the U.S. Census Bureau. The deficit increased from $92.8 billion in July (revised) to $105.6 billion in August, as imports increased more than exports. The goods deficit increased $12.8 billion in August to $136.6 billion. The services surplus increased less than $0.1 billion in August to $31.0 billion.

How Does Investment in a Skilled Workforce Impact the Nation’s Growth?

October 5, 2026 | The BEA Wire

A blog post from BEA Director Vipin Arora

I’d be willing to bet that the most effective and innovative places you’ve worked have had one thing in common: Great people. That’s certainly been my experience at BEA. While we make use of some remarkable technology, it’s really our people’s expertise and creativity—their human capital—that allows us to produce so many high-quality statistics.

It is understood that many users create ‘bookmarks’ or ‘favorites’ for their most frequently accessed pages on our site. However, due to some alterations to our directory structure, some ‘bookmarked’ URLs may no longer house the information they did prior to any redesign.

The links provided below will assist you in locating information within the BEA site. Should you be unable to locate the information you want, please contact us at webmaster@bea.gov and let us know the web page you were looking for.
